arXiv:2005.08831v4 [math.PR] 12 Oct 2020

On time inhomogeneous stochastic Itô equations with drift in Ld+1L_{d+1}

N.V. Krylov Email address: nkrylov@umn.edu Address: 127 Vincent Hall, University of Minnesota, Minneapolis, MN, 55455 To the memory of A.V. Skorokhod
Abstract.

We prove the solvability of Itô stochastic equations with uniformly nondegenerate, bounded, measurable diffusion and drift in Ld+1​(ℝd+1)L_{d+1}(\mathbb{R}^{d+1}). Actually, the powers of summability of the drift in xx and tt could be different. Our results seem to be new even if the diffusion is constant. The method of proving the solvability belongs to A.V. Skorokhod. Weak uniqueness of solutions is an open problem even if the diffusion is constant.

Key words and phrases: 
Itô’s equations with singular drift, Markov diffusion processes
2010 Mathematics Subject Classification
60H10, 60J60

1. Introduction

Let ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d} be a Euclidean space of points x=(x1,…,xd)x=(x^{1},...,x^{d}), d≥2d\geq 2. We fix some p,q∈[1,∞]p,q\in[1,\infty] such that

dp+1q≤1\frac{d}{p}+\frac{1}{q}\leq 1 (1.1)

with further restrictions on them to be specified later. The goal of this article is to study the solvability of Itô’s stochastic equations of the form

xt=x(0)+∫0tσ⁡(t(0)+s,xs)​d​ws+∫0tb⁡(t(0)+s,xs)​𝑑s,x_{t}=x^{(0)}+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma(t^{(0)}+s,x_{s})\,dw_{s}+\int_{0}^{t}b(t^{(0)}+s,x_{s})\,ds, (1.2)

where wtw_{t} is a dd-dimensional Wiener process, σ\sigma is a uniformly nondegenerate, bounded, Borel function with values in the set of symmetric d×dd\times d matrices, bb is a Borel measurable ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}- valued function given on (−∞,∞)×ℝd(-\infty,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^{d} such that

∫ℝ(∫ℝd|b⁡(t,x)|p​𝑑x)q/p​𝑑t<∞\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Big(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}|b(t,x)|^{p}\,dx\Big)^{q/p}\,dt<\infty (1.3)

if p≥qp\geq q or

∫ℝd(∫ℝ|b⁡(t,x)|q​𝑑t)p/q​𝑑x<∞\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\Big(\int_{\mathbb{R}}|b(t,x)|^{q}\,dt\Big)^{p/q}\,dx<\infty

if p≤qp\leq q. If p=∞p=\infty or q=∞q=\infty we interpret this conditions in a natural way. Observe that the case p=q=d+1p=q=d+1 is not excluded and in this case the condition becomes b∈Ld+1​(ℝd+1)b\in L_{d+1}(\mathbb{R}^{d+1}). Under this condition the solvability of (1.2) was proved in [4].

We are talking, of course, about weak solutions and prove their existence in Theorem 3.1. In Theorem 6.1 we prove the existence of strong Markov processes corresponding to diffusion σ\sigma and drift bb with the above properties. If bb is bounded, as we know from [17], there exist strong Markov and strong Feller processes with diffusion σ\sigma and drift bb for which the Harnack inequality holds and the caloric functions are Hölder continuous. We are far from proving such fine properties.

The main technical tools are collected in Section 4 where we prove new mixed norms estimates for the distributions of semimartingales. The treatment there, actually, follows very closely the work by A.I. Nazarov [12] written in terms of PDEs.

There is a vast literature about stochastic equations with irregular drift. Probably one of the first authors starting this area was N.I. Portenko, see his book [13], where he constructed diffusion processes with sufficiently regular σ\sigma and b∈Lp​(ℝd+1)b\in L_{p}(\mathbb{R}^{d+1}), p>d+2p>d+2. This condition on bb was later refined in many articles with various ambitious goals in them to the requirement that bb be such that (1.3) holds not under condition (1.1) but rather

dp+2q≤1.\frac{d}{p}+\frac{2}{q}\leq 1. (1.4)

We refer the reader to the recent articles [11], [2], [16] and the references therein for the discussion of many powerful results obtained under condition (1.4), when the case of equality is treated as “critical”. It could be critical in some respects but not for obtaining our results, that seem to be the first ones about the existence of solutions and Markov processes with our condition on the drift. Still it is worth emphasizing that our condition is different if p≥qp\geq q (and hence p≥d+1p\geq d+1) or p<qp<q, whereas there is no such distinction attached to (1.4).

We assume that d≥2d\geq 2 and denote

BR={x∈ℝd:|x|<R},Di=∂∂xi,Di​j=DiDj∂t=∂∂t.B_{R}=\{x\in\mathbb{R}^{d}:|x|<R\},\quad D_{i}=\frac{\partial}{\partial x^{i}},\quad D_{ij}=D_{i}D_{j}\quad\partial_{t}=\frac{\partial}{\partial t}.

For p,q∈[1,∞]p,q\in[1,\infty] we introduce the space Lp,qL_{p,q} as the space of Borel functions on ℝd+1\mathbb{R}^{d+1} such that

‖f‖p,qq:=∫ℝ(∫ℝd|f⁡(t,x)|p​𝑑x)q/p​𝑑t<∞\|f\|^{q}_{p,q}:=\int_{\mathbb{R}}\Big(\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}|f(t,x)|^{p}\,dx\Big)^{q/p}\,dt<\infty

if p≥qp\geq q or

‖f‖p,qp:=∫ℝd(∫ℝ|f⁡(t,x)|q​𝑑t)p/q​𝑑x<∞\|f\|^{p}_{p,q}:=\int_{\mathbb{R}^{d}}\Big(\int_{\mathbb{R}}|f(t,x)|^{q}\,dt\Big)^{p/q}\,dx<\infty

if p≤qp\leq q with natural interpretation of these definitions if p=∞p=\infty or q=∞q=\infty. To better memorize these formulas observe that pp is associated with integration with respect to xx, qq with that with respect to tt and the interior integral is always elevated to the power ≤1\leq 1. In case p=q=d+1p=q=d+1 we abbreviate Ld+1,d+1=Ld+1L_{d+1,d+1}=L_{d+1}, ∥⋅∥d+1,d+1=∥⋅∥d+1\|\cdot\|_{d+1,d+1}=\|\cdot\|_{d+1}.

3. An existence theorem

In this section we state a result saying that in a wide class of cases there exists a probability space and a Wiener process on this space such that a stochastic equation having measurable coefficients as well as this Wiener process is solvable. In other words, according to conventional terminology, we are talking here about “weak” solutions of a stochastic equation. The main difference between “weak” solutions and usual (“strong”) solutions consists in the fact that the latter can be constructed on any a priori given probability space on the basis of any given Wiener process.

Let σ⁡(t,x)\sigma(t,x) be Borel d×dd\times d symmetric matrix valued, b⁡(t,x)b(t,x) be Borel ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}-valued functions given on ℝd+1:=(−∞,∞)×ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d+1}:=(-\infty,\infty)\times\mathbb{R}^{d}. We assume that the eigenvalues of σ⁡(t,x)\sigma(t,x) are between δ\delta and δ−1\delta^{-1}, where δ∈(0,1)\delta\in(0,1) is a fixed number. The set of such matrices we denote by 𝕊δ\mathbb{S}_{\delta}.

Next, fix numbers p,q∈(1,∞)p,q\in(1,\infty), ‖b‖∈(0,∞)\|b\|\in(0,\infty) and let bn​(t,x)b^{n}(t,x), n=1,2,…n=1,2,..., be ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}-valued Borel functions on ℝ+d+1\mathbb{R}^{d+1}_{+} and suppose that

‖b‖p,q,‖bn‖p,q≤‖b‖,n=1,2,…,dp+1q=1\|b\|_{p,q},\|b^{n}\|_{p,q}\leq\|b\|,\quad n=1,2,...,\quad\frac{d}{p}+\frac{1}{q}=1

and bn→bb^{n}\to b as n→∞n\to\infty in Lp,qL_{p,q}. Let σn​(t,x)\sigma^{n}(t,x), n=1,2,…n=1,2,..., be Borel functions on ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d} with values in 𝕊δ\mathbb{S}_{\delta} such that σn→σ\sigma^{n}\to\sigma as n→∞n\to\infty (ℝd+1\mathbb{R}^{d+1}-a.e.).

Theorem 3.1.

Take (t0,x0)∈ℝd+1(t^{0},x^{0})\in\mathbb{R}^{d+1}. (i) There exists a probability space (Ω,ℱ,P)(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P), a filtration of σ\sigma-fields ℱt⊂ℱ\mathcal{F}_{t}\subset\mathcal{F}, t≥0t\geq 0, a process wtw_{t}, t≥0t\geq 0, which is a dd-dimensional Wiener process relative to {ℱt}\{\mathcal{F}_{t}\}, and an ℱt\mathcal{F}_{t}-adapted process xtx_{t} such that (a.s.) for all t≥0t\geq 0 equation (1.2) holds.

(ii) Furthermore, let (tn,xn)∈ℝd+1(t^{n},x^{n})\in\mathbb{R}^{d+1}, n=1,2,…n=1,2,..., and let (tn,xn)→(t0,x0)(t^{n},x^{n})\to(t^{0},x^{0}) as n→∞n\to\infty. Assume that for each n=1,2,…n=1,2,... there exists a probability space (Ωn,ℱn,Pn)(\Omega^{n},\mathcal{F}^{n},P^{n}), a filtration of σ\sigma-fields ℱtn⊂ℱn\mathcal{F}^{n}_{t}\subset\mathcal{F}^{n}, t≥0t\geq 0, a process wtnw^{n}_{t}, t≥0t\geq 0, which is a dd-dimensional Wiener process relative to {ℱtn}\{\mathcal{F}^{n}_{t}\}, and an ℱtn\mathcal{F}^{n}_{t}-adapted process xtnx^{n}_{t} such that (a.s.) for all t≥0t\geq 0

xtn=xn+∫0tσn​(tn+s,xsn)​d​wsn+∫0tbn​(tn+s,xsn)​𝑑s.x^{n}_{t}=x^{n}+\int_{0}^{t}\sigma^{n}(t^{n}+s,x^{n}_{s})\,dw^{n}_{s}+\int_{0}^{t}b^{n}(t^{n}+s,x^{n}_{s})\,ds. (3.1)

Then the finite dimensional distributions of a subsequence of x⋅nx^{n}_{\cdot} converge weakly to the corresponding distributions of one of the solutions of (1.2) described in (i). Moreover, if p≥qp\geq q, the set of distributions of x⋅nx^{n}_{\cdot} on C⁡([0,∞),ℝd)C([0,\infty),\mathbb{R}^{d}) is tight.

The proof of this theorem, following a similar proof by A.V. Skorokhod, is given in Section 5, after we make a crucial step in the next section where we prove, in particular, that for solutions of (1.2), any Borel f≥0f\geq 0, and T∈(0,∞)T\in(0,\infty)

E​∫0Tf⁡(t,xt)​𝑑t≤N​‖f‖p,q,E\int_{0}^{T}f(t,x_{t})\,dt\leq N\|f\|_{p,q}, (3.2)

where NN is independent of ff and (t0,x0)(t^{0},x^{0}).

It is worth saying that deciding whether the solutions of (1.2) are weakly unique or not under our conditions is a very challenging open problem even if σi​j≡δi​j\sigma^{ij}\equiv\delta^{ij}.

Remark 3.1.

Theorem 3.1 is also true if d/p+1/q<1d/p+1/q<1. This can be seen from its proof which becomes somewhat more technical in that case because of the form of our main estimate (4.9). Also the main interest in Theorem 3.1 is, of course, the lowest local integrability of bb, when the condition d/p+1/q=1d/p+1/q=1 is weaker than d/p+1/q<1d/p+1/q<1 due to Hölder’s inequality.

4. Estimates of the distributions of semimartingales

Here we first prove a version of Lemma 5.1 of [7]. The proof given in [7] uses somewhat advanced knowledge of very powerful results from the theory of fully nonlinear parabolic equations. We give a proof based on a simpler fact which in turn was one of the cornerstones of that theory.

Let (Ω,ℱ,P)(\Omega,\mathcal{F},P) be a complete probability space, let ℱt,t≥0\mathcal{F}_{t},t\geq 0, be an increasing family of complete σ\sigma-fields ℱt⊂ℱ\mathcal{F}_{t}\subset\mathcal{F}, t≥0t\geq 0, let mtm_{t} be an ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}-valued continuous local martingale relative to ℱt\mathcal{F}_{t}, let AtA_{t} be a continuous ℱt\mathcal{F}_{t}-adapted nondecreasing process, let BtB_{t} be a continuous ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}-valued ℱt\mathcal{F}_{t}-adapted process which has finite variation (a.e.) on each finite time interval. Assume that

A0=0,m0=B0=0,d​⟨m⟩t≪d​AtA_{0}=0,\quad m_{0}=B_{0}=0,\quad d\langle m\rangle_{t}\ll dA_{t}

and that we are also given progressively measurable relative to ℱt\mathcal{F}_{t} nonnegative processes rtr_{t} and ctc_{t}. Finally, take an ℱ0\mathcal{F}_{0} measurable ℝd\mathbb{R}^{d}-valued x0x_{0} and introduce

xt=x0+mt+Bt,τt=∫0trs​d​As,ϕt=∫0tcs​d​As,ati​j=12​d​⟨mi,mj⟩td​At.x_{t}=x_{0}+m_{t}+B_{t},\quad\tau_{t}=\int_{0}^{t}r_{s}\,dA_{s},\quad\phi_{t}=\int_{0}^{t}c_{s}\,dA_{s},\quad a^{ij}_{t}=\frac{1}{2}\frac{d\langle m^{i},m^{j}\rangle_{t}}{dA_{t}}.
Lemma 4.1.

Let γ\gamma be an ℱt\mathcal{F}_{t}-stopping time and set

A=E​∫0γe−ϕt​tr​as​d​At,B=E​∫0γe−ϕt​|d​Bt|.A=E\int_{0}^{\gamma}e^{-\phi_{t}}\text{\rm tr}\,a_{s}\,dA_{t},\quad B=E\int_{0}^{\gamma}e^{-\phi_{t}}\,|dB_{t}|.

Then for any Borel f⁡(t,x)≥0f(t,x)\geq 0 we have

E​∫0γe−ϕt​(rt​detat)1/(d+1)​f​(τt,xt)​d​AtE\int_{0}^{\gamma}e^{-\phi_{t}}(r_{t}\det a_{t})^{1/(d+1)}f(\tau_{t},x_{t})\,dA_{t}
≤N⁡(d)​(B2+A)d/(2​d+2)​‖f‖d+1.\leq N(d)(B^{2}+A)^{d/(2d+2)}\|f\|_{d+1}. (4.1)

Proof. Without losing generality we may assume that A<∞A<\infty and B<∞B<\infty. Furthermore, just stopping the processes AtA_{t}, mtm_{t}, and BtB_{t} at time γ\gamma, we reduce the general case to the one in which γ=∞\gamma=\infty. In that case we also observe that, as usual, it suffices to prove (4.1) for f∈C0∞​(ℝd+1)f\in C^{\infty}_{0}(\mathbb{R}^{d+1}).

After these reductions we use Theorem 2.2.4 of [9] according to which, for any λ>0\lambda>0 on ℝd+1\mathbb{R}^{d+1}, there exists a nonnegative function v⁡(t,x)v(t,x) such that

6. Markov processes corresponding to σ,b\sigma,b

We are going to use the results in [5] applied in the case when the semicompactum EE is ℝd+1\mathbb{R}^{d+1}, that is when the tt-variable is considered just as one of coordinates of points (t,x)∈ℝd+1(t,x)\in\mathbb{R}^{d+1}.

What remains is to prove that for (𝖳,𝒩t)({\sf T},\mathcal{N}_{t}) and ([0,∞),𝒩t+)([0,\infty),\mathcal{N}_{t+}) the conditions 2) and 3) are satisfied of the definition of Markov system in [5].
